..
An area of monsoon showers is moving in, but the cloud tops on it 
are warming. So the forecast is for it to peter out after reaching 
Guam. Not a very high confidence forecast, since it may not even 
reach Guam. So the forecast for Guam has numerous showers tonight, a 
high PoP low QPF type scenario, while the CNMI has isolated. Starting
Saturday, everyone adjusts back to scattered.

There isn't that much lightning around, and there isn't that much 
potential until you get way back near Yap. Nevertheless, went with a 
moderate risk of lightning all week, just broad brushed it to cover 
any short lived convective flare-ups.

Marine...
Sea heights will edge up a little next week, but probably only a 
little, unless a tropical cyclone spins up more than expected or 
something.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Etau (21W) is located near 25N167E, about 365 miles 
north of Wake Island. As of 0300Z, TS Etau is moving north-northwest 
at 13 mph. Near its center, maximum sustained winds are 50 mph, and 
its maximum sustained wave height is 20 ft, according to the Joint 
Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). It is expected to maintain this 
general course and speed through Saturday, continuing to move away 
from Wake Island and over open ocean. This general forecast track 
could take Etau north of 25N and out of our region by tonight.

Tropical Storm Bang-Lang (20W) is located near 19N165E, about 100 
miles west-southwest of Wake Island and moving northeast at 12 mph. 
TS Bang-Lang has increased with maximum sustained winds near its 
center now at 70 mph. Its maximum significant wave height is 20 ft 
according to the JTWC. Bang-Lang is forecast to intensify through 
Saturday night, possibly becoming a typhoon tonight. It will then 
begin to weaken as it starts subtropical transition. It is expected 
to make a turn toward the north-northeast with a slight increase in 
forward speed through Saturday. This general forecast track will take
Bang-Lang rather close to Wake Island this evening before heading 
over open ocean to the north.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO headers WTPN32 PGTW and WTPN33 PGTW
and from the National Weather Service under WMO headers WTPQ32 PGUM
and WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery depicts partly cloudy skies and isolated showers
across Pohnpei and Kosrae, and mostly cloudy skies with scattered
showers across Majuro, especially in southern coastal waters. 
Scatterometry shows gentle winds across Pohnpei, and light to gentle 
winds over Kosrae and Majuro. An active phase of the monsoon trough 
is forecasted through the weekend, so shower potential tops out at 50
percent with isolated thunderstorms for Pohnpei and Kosrae. Heavier 
showers with convective gusts look to be more of a possibility for 
Pohnpei, so additional wording was included for Sunday. As for
Majuro, diffusive flow will continue over the atolls, bringing light
to gentle winds, but showers will increase over the weekend. Drier 
weather is possible next week, but scattered showers are sparsely
included in the forecast as the monsoon trough remains active 
nearby.

Altimetry and buoy data indicates combined seas of 4 to 6 ft across 
the region with primary swell directions out of the west, southeast,
and east at Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Majuro, respectively. As for Kosrae,
surf is no longer considered elevated along south-facing reefs with 
an estimated height of 5 ft, so the headline will be discontinued 
for the time-being. However, these heights are still capable of a 
moderate risk of rip currents, so beachgoers should remain vigilant 
in or near the waters.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered showers across Chuuk and isolated 
showers across Palau and Yap. Altimetry shows combined seas ranging 
between 4 and 6 feet across the region. 

Overall, weather conditions have cleared up significantly across 
western Micronesia over the last 18 hours. Scattered showers are 
seen across the southern coastal waters of Chuuk and a stray 
isolated thunderstorm is observed in the northwest coastal waters of 
Yap. Isolated light showers were added back into Palau's forecast 
for the next few days based on satellite imagery showing weak 
squalls moving across Palau and further upstream to the southwest. 
Dry conditions will prevail across Palau through the period and 
across Yap through Sunday night. A tropical disturbance may bring 
scattered showers to Yap next week, but shower coverage will be 
greatly dependent on the location and organization of the 
disturbance. 

An active stretch is expected across Chuuk over the coming days as a 
tropical disturbance develops to the north. Locally heavy rainfall 
and gusty winds are expected this weekend across Chuuk. Some 
uncertainty remains on the development of this tropical disturbance 
based on current observations, but models are generally in agreement 
on an increase in showers and thunderstorms.
